overall: The AG found neither the Board nor the ZBA violated the Open Meeting Law as alleged: the ZBA's Sept. 28 notice was sufficiently specific, and the remaining allegations (reversal grounds, Board chair's conduct, ethics, new supplemental claims) were outside the law or not properly before it.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the ZBA's Sept. 28 meeting notice was too vague because it did not reference the Secretary's Sept. 26 letter about the Project.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the ZBA was not required to reference the Tepper letter in the notice for the September 28 meeting, where it otherwise adequately described the topic to be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complaints said ZBA member and chair gave no reasoning and identified no material change to justify reversing a prior ZBA decision.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review allegations that the ZBA did not have grounds to reverse its prior decision.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Board chair drafted the Sept. 27 Board meeting notice without public or Board input to pressure the ZBA into reversing itself.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to review the allegation that the Board chair improperly pressured the ZBA to reverse itself and improperly failed to seek input from the public or other Board members in preparation of the notice of the September 27 Board meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged ethical violations, which the AG treated as outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, to the extent they are properly part of the complaints, we also decline to review allegations of ethical violations.

allegations.summary: The complainant's Nov. 14 supplemental email raised new allegations not included in the original complaints.
allegations.key_passage: Our office will address only allegations made in an Open Meeting Law complaint in order to give the public body an opportunity to respond to those allegations.
